housing.summary: Espoo is part of the Helsinki metropolitan area and has among the highest rents in Finland, slightly below Helsinki. One-bedroom flats in central districts such as Tapiola and Leppavaara typically rent for roughly EUR 900-1,100/month. Deposits of one to three months' rent are standard.

banking.summary: Opening a Finnish bank account generally requires a Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus), a valid passport or national ID, a residence permit for non-EU/EEA nationals, and proof of address or employment. Major retail banks operating in Espoo include Nordea, OP (Osuuspankki), Danske Bank and S-Pankki.

schools.summary: Espoo provides Finnish- and Swedish-language comprehensive schools following the Finnish national core curriculum, plus English-language and international options such as Espoo International School and private IB schools. Schooling is compulsory and municipally organised.

legal_admin.summary: New residents must register their move and obtain a Finnish personal identity code and municipality of residence at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV). Non-EU/EEA nationals must first secure a residence permit from the Finnish Immigration Service (Migri) before registering.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register residence and obtain a personal identity code at DVV (Digital and Population Data Services Agency)

tax_finance.summary: The Finnish Tax Administration (Vero) issues the tax card (verokortti) needed for employment and withholds progressive income tax. New arrivals request a tax card and, where relevant, a tax number from Vero once they have a personal identity code.
tax_finance.tax_id_name: Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus) / tax card (verokortti)

transport.summary: Espoo is served by HSL (Helsinki Region Transport): buses, the Lansimetro metro extension, commuter trains and trams, all on one regional ticketing system shared with Helsinki and Vantaa. Zone fares apply (Espoo sits in zones B and C).
transport.network_name: HSL (Helsingin seudun liikenne / Helsinki Region Transport)
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA driving licences are valid in Finland; non-EU/EEA licences may be exchanged or must be re-taken depending on the issuing country. Licence exchange is handled by Traficom (Finnish Transport and Communications Agency).
transport.healthcare_registration: Register for public healthcare through your municipality/wellbeing services county of residence once you hold a personal identity code; national health and social insurance coverage is administered by Kela (Social Insurance Institution of Finland).
